problem: "Bottom-up integration starts at the leaf drivers and drives them with test programs" confuses the two standard integration aids. A driver is the test program, not a module; bottom-up integration starts at the lowest-level (leaf) modules and tests them using drivers, while stubs are used in top-down integration. As written, a student would write "leaf drivers" in the exam and lose marks.
fix: Bottom-up integration starts at the leaf modules (the lowest-level drivers and hardware-access routines) and tests them with drivers, which are small test programs that call the module under test and supply its inputs. Top-down integration instead starts at the main control flow and replaces missing lower modules with stubs.

where: Section 3, first paragraph, and Exam trap 3
problem: Verification is defined as checking that "each artifact match[es] the stage before it". That holds for a strict waterfall handover, but it contradicts the V-model rule given in Section 2, where a system test verifies against the specification written several stages earlier and an acceptance test verifies against the requirements. The definition is too narrow.
fix: Verification asks whether the product is being built right: does each artifact match the specification it was derived from (for a test level in the V-model, the design level it is paired with)? Validation asks whether the right product is being built: does the finished system meet the customer's need?

problem: T_total = sum of the stage weeks is only true when the stages run one after another. On a real Gantt chart with overlap the sum double-counts the overlapping weeks, and the formula says nothing about this. It also leaves out maintenance without saying so, while the stage list above it has maintenance as a stage.
fix: Add: this sum holds only for sequential (non-overlapping) stages; for each overlap of n weeks between two adjacent stages, subtract n weeks once. State that maintenance is excluded because T_total is measured to customer delivery.

problem: The figure note on architecture reads "design 3 weeks", but the worked example gives specification and architecture together as 3 weeks. A student adding the figure notes gets the right total by luck, but the note misstates which stages the 3 weeks cover.
fix: Change the specification node note to "2 weeks"... no: keep requirements at 2 weeks and label the architecture node "spec + architecture: 3 weeks" so the figure matches the worked example.
